wy_3_mytho_wall.blurb: Mytho Wall is the third wall you meet on the hike up through the Shipyard, a steep sport crag in Piney Creek Canyon in the Eastern Big Horns. All fifteen routes are bolted, and the grades start at 5.11 and run into the low 5.13s, with most of the lines in the 5.12 range. Expect overhanging walls of pockets, with some of the finishes being abrupt and awkward. The wall holds shade through the morning in summer, so spring and fall are the comfortable seasons. A big tree at the base gives a shady place to hang out between lines. This is a place for strong, pumpy climbing, not for a first lead day.

wy_aspen_glade_the.blurb: The Aspen Glade makes up the left-hand part of the Gun Street cliff band in the Wild Iris area above Lander, at roughly 9,000 feet. It is a sport crag with fifteen routes on clean, long limestone walls that lean back just short of vertical. Grades center on 5.11 and 5.12, with a couple of 5.10s and a single route in the 5.13 range, so it suits climbers already comfortable on harder pocketed rock. The cliff faces roughly south and has few trees, so it gets a lot of sun; mornings and evenings offer some shade, and one overhanging block holds shade nearly all day. Expect quiet and big views, since most visitors stay on the closer walls.

wy_c_wild_horses_wall.blurb: Wild Horses Wall is a sport crag at the far west end of the Main Wall at Wild Iris near Lander, the third section from the left. It holds fifteen bolted routes: one easy 5.8, then a spread that runs from 5.10 through 5.12, with a single route in the 5.13 range. That makes it a reasonable stop for climbers working through the 5.10s and 5.11s. The face looks south and can be warm on summer afternoons, though there is plenty of shade at the base. Plan on a long walk of around half an hour from the parking lot, which keeps the crowds thinner than at the closer sections.

wy_happy_wheel_wall.blurb: Happy Wheel Wall is a sport wall in Sinks Canyon near Lander, sitting about halfway between the left and right branches of the trail up to the Main Wall. It is the next wall along after Camel Jockey Wall when you move right to left. The fifteen bolted routes cover an unusually wide range, from a 5.8 and a 5.9 up through the 5.10s and 5.11s to a pair of climbs in the 5.13 range, so a mixed group can find something each. Sinks Canyon is known for sport climbing on limestone and for staying climbable through much of the year, with the sun-facing side of the canyon warm on cold days.

wy_head_games.blurb: Head Games is a sizable cluster of boulders at the bottom of Strube Loop on Casper Mountain, in the Skunk Hollow area. It offers fifteen problems and nothing else, split between the Motor Skills and Decapitation sectors. Most are short problems on slight overhangs with slopey holds, with a few low mantels, small boulders and a traverse. The grades sit mainly between V0 and V3, with one much harder V6. The setting is cooler than the lowlands in summer and has plenty of shade. A trail now runs through the boulders, and people are asked to leave the dead trees where they lie so nothing slides downhill.

wy_lower_vegas_wall.blurb: Lower Vegas Wall is one of the sectors on the south side of the river in Shoshone Canyon, a few miles west of Cody. It is mainly a sport wall, with fourteen bolted lines and one trad route among the fifteen. Grades start around 5.10 and run up to the low 5.13s, concentrated in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, so it is better for intermediates and up than for beginners. The canyon floor climbing is generally best in spring and fall and comfortable for much of the summer, though the south-side walls across the water can feel chilly in cooler weather.

wy_rendezvous_buttress.blurb: Rendezvous Buttress sits on the Southwest Ridge of Reese Mountain in the Laramie Range, at about 6,550 feet, in the Hightower area. It takes up the stretch to the right of the ridge's southwesternmost corner. The fifteen climbs are a mix of sport and trad routes, with seven of each plus one aid line. Free grades run from 5.9 to 5.11, mostly in the 5.10 range, so it suits climbers looking for moderate to middling lines. One slab on the buttress faces south. Reaching it takes a hike uphill north from the confluence of the creeks to the ridge corner.

wy_sandstone_buttress.blurb: Sandstone Buttress is the first large formation you reach when entering Sinks Canyon near Lander, and it rises about 250 feet. The fine-grained sandstone gives decent friction and is kind on the hands. Most of the fifteen routes here are trad, with a handful of sport lines, and grades stretch from 5.6 up to 5.13, with the easier end well represented by multi-pitch lines. The short walk from the pull-off puts you on the first ledge in a couple of minutes. Because most climbers drive on to the limestone further up the canyon, this wall tends to be fairly empty.
